q: When light is incident on the surface of an object some of the light is sent back and this phenomenon is called ____.
e: Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface.

q: A ray of light is a path along which the light ____.
e: A ray represents the direction of light propagation.

q: A beam of light is a collection of ____.
e: Multiple rays together form a light beam.

q: Searchlights used in trains and lighthouses emit ____.
e: These devices produce collimated (parallel) light beams for long-distance visibility.

q: A beam emitted by a light bulb is a ____.
e: Light from a point source like a bulb spreads out radially.

q: In Figure 8.4, a ray which represents the incident light is an ____.
e: The incoming ray before reflection is called the incident ray.

q: A line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence is called ____.
e: The normal is an imaginary reference line used in reflection geometry.

q: A ray which represents the reflected light is a ____.
e: The outgoing ray after bouncing off the surface is the reflected ray.

q: An angle between the incident ray and the normal is an ____.
e: This angle measures how far the incident ray deviates from the normal.

q: An angle between the reflected ray and the normal is an ____.
e: This angle describes the direction of the reflected ray relative to the normal.

q: The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same ____.
e: All three elements are coplanar, which is the first law of reflection.

q: The angle of incidence is equal to the ____.
e: This equality is the second law of reflection and holds for all smooth surfaces.

q: Laws of reflection are true for all reflecting surfaces for plane mirrors as well as ____.
e: Both flat and curved reflective surfaces obey the same fundamental reflection laws.
